subject.title: fix(workboard): release path for legacy claims without ownerId

question: For a legacy claim that has an `agent_id` but no valid current claim token, should Doctor clear the claim as unrecoverable, or should OpenClaw introduce an explicit administrator recovery mechanism that establishes a usable authorization state?
rationale: A claim token is part of the current authorization boundary, and inventing one without a way for a legitimate actor to obtain it does not define safe recovery semantics.

options.title: Clear unrecoverable legacy claims
options.body: Clear any legacy claim that lacks a verifiable canonical token so the card safely returns to the dispatch queue.

options.title: Design explicit administrative recovery
options.body: Retain ownership only if maintainers define a deliberate admin recovery flow that creates and exposes a usable authorization state without weakening normal claim checks.

recommendation.title: Clear unrecoverable legacy claims
recommendation.body: Clear any legacy claim that lacks a verifiable canonical token so the card safely returns to the dispatch queue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision belongs with the people responsible for current Workboard ownership and mutation semantics.
